nice_guideline_used: CG181 / PH46 / NG28 (cardiovascular risk, obesity, prediabetes) and NG136 (hypertension)

medications.purpose: Essential hypertension; renal protection in CKD risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension and CKD protection

medications.purpose: Add‑on therapy for hypertension to achieve BP target <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 supports CCB as second‑line when BP not at target with ACE‑I alone

medications.dose: 500 mg once daily with evening meal (titrate to 500 mg twice daily after 1 week if tolerated)
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity and reduce progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28/PH38 recommends metformin for high‑risk prediabetes (BMI ≥30 kg/m², hypertension, HbA1c 6.2%)

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in metabolic syndrome (QRISK ≥10%)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 advises statin therapy for anyone with ≥10% 10‑year CVD risk

medications.dose: 100 mg four times daily (q6h) with food
medications.duration: 3 days (if symptoms resolve) or 5 days max for uncomplicated cystitis
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG109 recommends nitrofurantoin as first‑line for uncomplicated lower UTI in women

interactions_checked.interaction: No clinically significant interaction; monitor renal function as both affect kidneys
interactions_checked.action: Check eGFR before starting metformin and repeat after 2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can modestly increase atorvastatin levels but risk of myopathy is low at 20 mg
interactions_checked.action: Baseline CK and LFTs; monitor for muscle symptoms

interactions_checked.interaction: Nitrofurantoin may cause a transient rise in serum creatinine; no direct pharmacokinetic interaction
interactions_checked.action: Ensure eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² before prescribing and re‑check renal labs after 3 days

contraindications.reason: Current acute urinary tract infection increases risk of genital infection and urosepsis
contraindications.alternative: Delay SGLT2i until UTI resolved and eGFR confirmed ≥45

contraindications.reason: Would increase fluid retention; patient has hypertension and possible early CKD
contraindications.alternative: Avoid; consider GLP‑1 RA later if weight loss needed

contraindications.reason: Risk of lactic acidosis in severe renal impairment
contraindications.alternative: Do not start until eGFR confirmed ≥30; if eGFR 30‑45, start 500 mg once daily
Use fosfomycin 3 g single dose if renal function inadequate

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² for initial prescribing; must be measured before starting metformin and nitrofurantoin
Lipid profile not available – assumed QRISK ≥10% based on hypertension, obesity, prediabetes; formal QRISK calculation required
Allergy status unknown – verify no sulfonamide or nitrofurantoin allergy before prescribing
Pregnancy status not documented – assume not pregnant; confirm negative pregnancy test if of child‑bearing potential before starting metformin or statin
Urine culture not performed – if symptoms persist >48 h, obtain culture and consider alternative antibiotic
treatment_summary: The plan addresses metabolic syndrome by initiating metformin for insulin resistance, atorvastatin for cardiovascular risk reduction, and reinforcing lifestyle change (diet, exercise, weight‑loss programme). Hypertension is already controlled with lisinopril and amlodipine per NICE NG136. Acute cystitis is treated with a short course of nitrofurantoin. Monitoring includes renal function, liver enzymes, CK, HbA1c, lipid profile, and blood pressure, with follow‑up in 2‑3 weeks to review labs, UTI resolution, and drug tolerance.
